offence_severity: Minimum 10 years, maximum life imprisonment or death
key_evidence_accepted: The letter dated 16-02-2004 allegedly written by the deceased to her brother (PW-3) was the only evidence produced by the prosecution to prove that the appellants had subjected the victim to harassment and cruelty in connection with demand for dowry.
witness_credibility: The court expressed grave doubts about the authenticity of the letter written by the deceased to PW-3 and questioned the credibility of the evidence provided by PW-3, noting that he did not specifically state the deceased was at Ahmedabad on 16-02-2004.
bail_history: Appellants are on bail and their bail bonds are discharged
trial_duration: Dates of offence: 18-05-2004; Trial judgment: 04-12-2006; High Court decision: 04-12-2006; Supreme Court decision: 18-03-2013
legal_representation: Counsel for the accused: Haresh Raichura, Saroj Raichura, Kalp Raichura, Ranvir Singh, Rajat Vats; Counsel for the State: D. Hemantika Wahi, Pinky Behara, Shubhade Deshpande
appeal_history: Trial court: Conviction; High Court: Affirmed conviction; Supreme Court: Appeal allowed, conviction set aside
prosecution_argument: The prosecution argued that the appellants (husband and in-laws) had subjected the deceased to cruelty and harassment for dowry and had instigated her to commit suicide.
defence_argument: The defence argued that the deceased was in Chaksiriya village with her brother's family in Bihar and was not at Ahmedabad on 16-02-2004, and that she committed suicide because she wanted to remain with her parents and not live with the appellants.
legal_principle_applied: The Court applied the principle that the prosecution must prove beyond reasonable doubt that the husband or his relative subjected the deceased to cruelty or harassment in connection with dowry demands.
